title: Mem-World: Memory-Augmented Action-Conditioned World Models for Persistent Robot Manipulation
summary: Mem-World augments action-conditioned robot video world models with W-VMem, a wrist-view-centered 4D surfel memory that ties past observations to evolving scene surfaces so the model can retrieve geometry-relevant history despite occlusions and fast wrist-camera motion. In manipulation rollouts, this helps preserve scene details that ordinary current-frame models forget or hallucinate, improving policy evaluation over Ctrl-World with 14.5% higher Pearson correlation to real-world performance. Using its synthetic data for policy improvement also raises long-horizon task success from 58% to 72%.

extra.full_text: Action-conditioned world models have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot learning, offering a scalable alternative to costly real-world experimentation by generating action-consistent video rollouts. However, persistent world modeling remains challenging in manipulation: frequent end-effector occlusions and rapid wrist-camera motion make the current observation insufficient for predicting future views, causing models to forget or hallucinate scene details seen in earlier frames. Existing memory retrieval strategies often fail to identify informative history in dynamic manipulation scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose Mem-World, a memory-augmented multi-view action-conditioned world model. At its core, we present W-VMem, a 4D wrist-view-centered surfel-indexed memory that anchors historical observations to temporally evolving surface elements. By explicitly modeling when and where scene elements are observed, W-VMem enables geometry-aware retrieval of relevant history frames conditioned on future actions. During generation, relevant history frames are selected via surfel-based rendering and scoring, providing informative and non-redundant context for prediction. Extensive experiments show that Mem-World generates persistent rollouts in complex manipulation scenarios, enables more reliable policy evaluation than Ctrl-World, improving the Pearson correlation with real-world performance by 14.5\%, and supports effective policy improvement through synthetic data generation, increasing success rates from 58\% to 72\% on long-horizon tasks.

summary: Chinese humanoid robotics company ENGINEAI has reportedly filed confidentially for a Hong Kong IPO, with CICC and CITIC said to be supporting the share issuance. title: ‘STK 2026’ 달군 애지봇…전방위 로봇 응용 기술의 정수 선보여
summary: AGIBOT used STK 2026 in Seoul as its first major professional exhibition after entering the Korean market, showing a robot portfolio through live demos and hands-on experiences. The demonstrations emphasized motion control, human-robot interaction, and real task execution, positioning the company around broad robot-application capability rather than a single-purpose product.

title: “AI, 자동차·선박·로봇 몸을 입다”…산업부 '제5회 M.AX 콘퍼런스' 개최
summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy held the 5th M.AX Conference on June 18 focused on embodied AI, meaning AI that is built into physical systems such as cars, ships, robots, and industrial products. The event brought industry, academic, and research experts together to discuss how AI is moving beyond digital services into future vehicles, autonomous ships, AI semiconductors, and manufacturing, where the ability of products to perceive, decide, and act is increasingly tied to industrial competitiveness.

title: [게시판] 삼쩜삼, 전용 AI 라인업으로 고객 상담 9만건 처리 등 단신

title: KAIST, 6.7배 늘어나도 끄떡없는 차세대 자가발전 웨어러블 센서 개발
summary: KAIST researchers developed a self-powered wearable sensor that can stretch up to 668% while still producing stable electrical signals, targeting long-term monitoring of heart rate, breathing, and joint motion without batteries. The result points toward more practical electronic skin and soft-robot sensing, where devices need to deform like skin or soft materials while continuing to detect motion and external stimuli reliably.

title: 로봇 학습 데이터 스타트업 '엑스도프', 7000만달러 투자 유치
summary: XDOF, a startup focused on robot training data, emerged from stealth with a $70 million raise from Thrive Capital, Spark Capital, Lux, WndrCo, and others. The company is tackling a bottleneck in robotics: robots need large volumes of precise physical-interaction data to learn useful behavior, but ordinary video sources like YouTube or worker-shot footage are too low-fidelity for that purpose.
